segments.narration: Giant boulders move across this dry lakebed all by themselves. Deep trails stretch behind rocks weighing seven hundred pounds.
For decades, fresh tracks appeared every winter. Yet nobody ever caught a single stone in motion.
Were the stones breaking physics? Researchers finally bolted custom GPS trackers directly to the rocks and waited.
Rare winter rain formed thin ice sheets around the stones. Morning sun thawed the ice into floating panels, letting light breezes push the heavy rocks over slick mud.
In 2014, high-speed GPS finally solved it. But as Death Valley warms, will these walking rocks ever move again?
